title: Signed coordinate Cartier adjunct in the published orientation chart
statement:
Fix the finite purity datum P [def-pur-conventions] and a separated finite-type k-scheme T. On every level where the published affine-line datum is defined [def-pur-affine-line-datum], CoordinateCartierSign [def-pur-coordinate-section-cartier-sign] holds: the coordinate zero ideal is Cartier, there is OrientationSupportData with the stipulated normalized snake boundary, and a morphism pur from the coefficient unit to the published Gysin value whose support evaluation is the positive coordinate Kummer boundary and whose negative is precisely coordinateCartierAdjunct. All maps are the existing derived coordinate maps; no arbitrary orientation is chosen.

The exact Lean statement is:

theorem coordinateCartierBoundarySign (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u})
    (T : Scheme.{u}) (aT : T ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType aT] [QuasiCompact aT] [IsSeparated aT] :
    P.CoordinateCartierSign T aT

source.place: Rank-one supported Cartier normalization, even twists and finite etale-origin transport; expanded parent proof steps as specified below.

proof.text: The coordinate zero divisor is Cartier: locally t is a nonzerodivisor in R[t]. In its dual ideal take e=t^-1 and open divisor section tau=t*e. The unique ordinary supported Kummer boundary is the normalized relative torsor extension taking tau to zero, spliced with the Kummer extension and the roots coefficient map.

Apply the principal-torsor Yoneda sign formula with global frame e, open section tau and g=t. It gives minus the coordinate localization boundary. The relative cone has D(a,b)=(da,r(a)-db), whose connecting representative is (0,-b). Its support comparison and the roots coefficient map preserve that sign.

Use the affine-line orientation support chart and its normalized snake boundary. Exact site comparison, the actual closed adjunct-counit identity, and the single/shift comparisons defining coordinateCartierAdjunct carry the preceding equation to D.support.hom(gysinHomToSections(coordinateCartierAdjunct))=-D.coordinateBoundary. Negating this adjunct gives pur, and additive Hom evaluation gives the positive boundary; double negation proves the claimed equality. Empty schemes and coefficient characteristic two are included.
